The hello page is built: style.css has a dark theme, there's an index.html, and server.js uses node:http to serve those two files on `PORT` or 3000. The designer made index.html as well, because the server needs a page to serve.
- **Server:** it only serves `/`, `/index.html` and `/style.css`, so nothing else on disk can be reached. Any other path gets a 404, and a failed file read gets a 500.
- **Reviewer:** no bugs, no security issues, and every file is under 30 lines (27, 15 and 27). Two optional extras: return 405 for methods other than GET, and add an `X-Content-Type-Options` header.
- **Not run:** the backend agent wasn't allowed to use Bash, so no one has run server.js or `node --check`. The reviewer found no syntax errors by reading it, and it needs Node 16.9 or later.
- **Left:** run `node server.js` and open htt<path> to confirm the page loads with its styles.
